acceptanceCriteria: `corvint-tasks run --attempt` gains a detached mode whose command survives the launching session's exit while the attempt lease is held, keeps heartbeating, and stays fenced (killed if the attempt is fenced or reaped).
A later session for the same ticket and attempt can attach to the running command and read its RUN_OUTCOME once finished; output is retained in a bounded file.
Documentation states how this relates to CAL-V0-089 checkpointed continuation.
Maintained tests: launcher exits, command continues and completes, successor reads the outcome; fenced attempt kills the detached command.
body:
Filed 2026-10-06 from GitHub issue beamfall/corvint#627 (orchestrator triage; reporter observations on main-2fff511, not reproduced yet).

A long command run under an attempt dies with its session when the session hits its context or wall limit; a 23-minute suite was killed at test 23 and its results lost. Request: keep it running detached, heartbeating and fenced, and let the next session attach and read RUN_OUTCOME. Relate to #354 / CAL-V0-089 checkpointed continuation.

completion.reason: Delivered in PR beamfall/corvint#632, merged to main as 265835f77f9aca1175dfeac06ee7e63ecf17a805. Evidence: docs/build-log/2026-10-06-v1-0856-detached-attempt-run.md at that commit (the digest is that file's sha256), which records the change, the maintained tests the acceptance criteria name, the independent Codex review and its repairs. The batch head passed the doc gates, go vet, the full suites of the touched packages on darwin and every hosted CI check (go-product shards, doc-gates, go-interop). NOT_RUN: make gate, live multi-agent/dispatcher qualification and non-darwin execution where that entry says so.

title: corvint-tasks: let an attempt-bound long command outlive its agent session and be adopted by the next session for the ticket (issue #627)
